sources.title: Austrian Archaeological Institute: Urnfield Culture Networks
sources.note: Overview: thirteenth to eighth centuries BCE; related regional phenomena, cremation and metal exchange.

sources.title: Heiss and colleagues: The Hoard of the Rings, 2019
sources.note: Abstract, pit V5400 context and interpretation: cereal rings, barley/wheat, dried dough, uncertain use. Same article mirrored at PMC6550392; treated as one source.

sources.title: Austrian Archaeological Institute: Thunau am Kamp
sources.note: Late Bronze Age settlement about 1050 to 800 BCE; buildings, ovens, rock cellars; destruction 800/750 BCE. Medieval phases excluded.

sources.title: Austrian Archaeological Institute: Franzhausen-Kokoron cemetery
sources.note: 403 excavated graves; utensils, razors, food offerings and transition into Hallstatt period.

sources.title: Austrian Archaeological Institute: Resource curation, power and cult at Stillfried?
sources.note: Storage-pit geometry, charred seeds and deposits. Supraregional grain redistribution remains a research question; rituals interpreted, not witnessed.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The Bronze Age
sources.note: Danish chronology 1700 to 500 BCE; imported metals and elite oak-coffin burials.

sources.title: Earle and colleagues: Everyday Life at Bjerre Site 7, 2022
sources.note: Bjerre 7 dated to ninth century BCE; cooking evidence, amber and household craft. Authors distinguish debris disposal from activity locations.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The Egtved Girl
sources.note: 1370 BCE burial; cord skirt, tunic, comb, awl and hair net. No claim about disputed distant origin or child sacrifice adopted.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The Egtved Girl’s beer
sources.note: Bark bucket, residue and plant evidence; probable beer with honey, berries, wheat and bog myrtle. Modern recipe caption not treated as an ancient recipe.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: A folding chair from the Bronze Age
sources.note: Guldhøj chair, later fifteenth century BCE; ash wood, pitch inlay and fragmentary otter-skin seat.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: A small family?
sources.note: Borum Eshøj, wood felling 1351 BCE, three adults; kinship explicitly hypothetical.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The lurs and their music
sources.note: Bronze instrument structure, sounding originals and modern playing, not recovered ancient melodies.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The Sun Chariot
sources.note: Trundholm, about 1400 BCE; divine-horse and sun interpretation.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: Ship images in the Bronze Age
sources.note: Scandinavian ship imagery from about 1700 BCE; crew as lines, rock carving distribution. No deciphered written sentence claimed.

sources.title: National Museum of Denmark: The Early Iron Age
sources.note: Around 500 BCE local iron extraction and later periodisation. Does not imply immediate universal replacement of bronze.

sources.title: Reading Museum: The Silesian Collection, 2022
sources.note: Specific Muskau-area excavation account and collection, including children’s graves. General claims about peoples or cannibalism are not adopted.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Biskupin: Archaeological reserve
sources.note: Fortified settlement section: 106 houses, 13 rows, timber streets, defences and tree-ring dates. Neolithic longhouse and medieval settlement sections excluded.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Biskupin: History of research
sources.note: Datowanie section distinguishes earlier archaeological estimates from dendrochronology; discovery and interdisciplinary investigations.

sources.title: Moskal-del Hoyo and colleagues: Plant usage in the Carpathian Foothills, 2013
sources.note: Conference abstract, printed page 29, PDF page 29: six Bronze Age sites, common millet and firewood/weed evidence. Abstract-level evidence, no invented recipe.

sources.title: National Museum in Lublin: Miniature scoop 1664/A/ML/2
sources.note: Indexed institutional object record: Bielsko burial, miniature dimensions; toy and symbolic-vessel interpretations unresolved. Direct open failed.

sources.title: Justyna Żychlińska: Function of the Lusatian clay discs, 2015
sources.note: Academic abstract: competing utilitarian, play and ritual interpretations of clay discs. Do not select one as proven.

sources.title: Regional Museum in Bełchatów: Prehistory and history of the region
sources.note: Indexed institutional text, Hallstatt/La Tene transition and mixed Pomeranian/Cloche material. Later Przeworsk kilns and Roman coins excluded. Shared source budget across batch.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Poznań: Birds in Pomeranian culture
sources.note: Indexed complete section PTAKI W KULTURZE POMORSKIEJ checked. Direct PDF retrieval failed. Separate versus shared Cloche classification unresolved; cist reopening and decorations. Bird scarcity does not prove religious insignificance.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Poznań: Early Iron Age gallery
sources.note: Pomeranian beginnings mid-seventh century BCE; face-urn origins disputed; funerary use and cist construction. Gallery-wide 650 to 125 BCE is not adopted as exact lifetime.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Gdańsk: Early Iron Age Department
sources.note: Full indexed Polish institutional record read; exact captions distinguish Pomeranian from Lusatian and Wielkowiejska objects. Lisie Jamy ard only broadly early Iron Age. Biological-sex inference from aesthetic appearance explicitly rejected by museum.

sources.title: Szymon Modzelewski, Ostrowiec Museum: Pomeranian urn, 2023
sources.note: Domestic settlement and farming; rough-walled urn with unknown exact provenance; transition in late third century BCE. Unsupported detailed religious certainties in the source not adopted.

sources.title: Chojnice Museum: From Etruria to Pomerania? exhibition, 2009
sources.note: Exhibition of face urns, jewellery, tools and grooming equipment; funerary iconography. Source’s mid-sixth century start differs from Poznan’s mid-seventh: phase variation noted internally, no exact founding year asserted.

sources.title: Historical Museum in Legionowo: De Profundis
sources.note: Early Iron Age Cloche section: form, decoration, animal remains and settlements. Subsequent Przeworsk material on same page excluded.

sources.title: Historical Museum in Legionowo: Iron Age exhibition
sources.note: Opening paragraph and Stanisławów Pierwszy caption. 47 archaeological features, not 47 graves; tweezers, ornaments, horn and bone. Indexed text has encoding damage but terms and context recoverable.

sources.title: Kaczyński and Stanaszek: Warsaw Annopol Cloche-Grave cemetery, 2023
sources.note: Wiadomości Archeologiczne 74, pp. 191 to 201, DOI 10.36154/wa.74.2023.09. Primary article read in mirror https://bialczynski.pl/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Nieumyslne-spowodowanie.pdf because CEJSH PDF returned 403. Printed pages 198 to 199 skeletal findings and 201 summary; no reliance on host commentary.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Missing verified. Imported 1500 to 500 BCE; outlines extend Atlantic to central Europe and include Britain/Ireland. Conventional central European chronology narrower. Public caveat supplied; Austrian case studies explicitly local. No single ethnicity, language, sovereign or successor inferred.

Missing verified. HB 1500 to 500 BCE with early envelope 4.98 to 53.98E, 50.24 to 64.10N, grossly broader than Nordic Bronze Age. Public overview states restricted Danish/Scandinavian examples. No assumption of one culture throughout eastern polygon. Earlier 1700 BCE context clearly distinguished.

Missing verified. Map 700 to 500 BCE, outline broadly Polish/central European 14.834 to 22.678E49.354 to 54.725N. Wider culture predates this map. Public overview identifies archaeological rather than ethnic unit; Biskupin timber phase explicitly earlier than selected window. No continuity to modern Sorbs or Poles asserted.

Missing verified. HB 500 BCE to 200 CE; narrow northern Polish bbox 15.086 to 19.899 E, 52.592 to 54.834 N. Public late-end and distribution warnings included. Institutional chronologies differ: Poznań mid-seventh century, Chojnice mid-sixth, depending on phase/classification. No exact founding asserted. Separate Cloche card acknowledges debate. No medieval Pomeranian identity substitution.

Missing verified. HB 500 BCE to 200 CE; bbox 15.100 to 25.720 E, 48.826 to 53.825 N. Name, Polish location and dates support Cloche/Bell-Grave identity, not third-millennium BCE Bell Beaker. Pomeranian relationship is debated, so separate narrative with public qualification. Imported extent is not a certified distribution. Annopol English summary contains an apparently erroneous bare 375±30 number; not adopted, only the authors’ fifth-century BCE conclusion.
